prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1441; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On the reported date, I responded to a rear-end collision on a public roadway in Pasadena, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in a travel lane when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 1 stated that neck pain and stiffness began shortly after impact and reported whiplash symptoms at the scene. Driver 1 presented a policy card and insurance documents listing Driver 1 as the named insured on the vehicle. Driver 2 acknowledged following too closely and did not dispute the sequence of events. Two independent witnesses in nearby vehicles gave statements consistent with Driver 2 striking the rear of the stopped vehicle. Scene photographs show rear-end damage that is generally consistent with the described impact speed and direction. The vehicle's prior condition showed no earlier damage that I could identify or that either driver mentioned. A Passenger was present in the front seat. Driver 1's exact seating position at the moment of impact could not be fully established from statements and observations at the scene. Both drivers were advised of their reporting obligations, and no citation was issued at this time.
